newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby soybeans end sharply lower on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby soybeans end sharply lower on weather.

text.p: Forecasts showing U.S. Midwest temperatures climbing back to normal levels caused CBOT soybean futures to end with heavy losses on Monday, traders and analysts said.
"The sell-off today was technical but weather also had something to do with it," said Joel Karlin, analyst with Everen Securities. "We're supposed to get warmer temperatures."
High temperatures across the Corn Belt were expected to hit 80 degrees, which is slightly below normal, forecasters said.
Typically, weather usually only affects the new crop contracts, but traders said the forecast's reach had expanded to old crop contracts.
"I know it doesn't make sense, but it's all weather, weather, weather," said a veteran trader.
Liquidation following Friday's Commitments of Traders report from the CFTC also pressured the nearby contracts, traders said.
Technical selling was cited as another source of weakness. July soybeans pierced key support at $8.21 per bushel, which triggered a wave of sell-stop orders, traders said.
CBOT July soybeans ended down 24-1/4 cent per bushel at $8.11 and other months were 7-3/4 to 17-1/4 cents lower.
